key_insight: A hybrid translator combines deterministic compilation and LLM agents to convert quantum MLIR dialects into QIR, with independent simulator testing to check behavioral agreement.
engineering_relevance: The approach could reduce quantum compiler integration work across frameworks, although the abstract does not evaluate materials science applications.
method: Use deterministic translation for known Catalyst and Quake grammars.
Route unseen dialects to LLM agents and invoke repair when deterministic output fails testing.
Compare source and translated output distributions using dual-backend simulation and total variation distance.
evidence_signal: Across 41 circuits spanning three dialects and 1–100 qubits, deterministic translation was gate-exact on all 70 circuit–dialect pairs with average TVD similarity above 95%; four of six models generated valid logical-level QIR for the unseen FTQC dialect on the first iteration.
watch_item: Valid QIR and simulator distribution agreement do not establish full semantic correctness or reliable generalization to arbitrary unseen dialects.
paper_title: Agentic MLIR-to-QIR Translation with Dual-Backend Testing: A Hybrid Deterministic and LLM Approach
